Empty stomach: >=1 h before or 2 h after food
Can cause fetal harm; avoid, use contraception
Monitor function; PK in impairment unknown
Avoid; use alcohol-free emollients for skin
LFTs, renal function/electrolytes, INR if on warfarin, pulmonary symptoms
summary: Erlotinib is an oral reversible EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor for EGFR exon 19 deletion / exon 21 (L858R) mutated metastatic NSCLC and (with gemcitabine) advanced pancreatic cancer. Dosed once daily on an empty stomach. Major safety concerns are interstitial lung disease and hepatotoxicity, plus characteristic rash and diarrhea.
indications: Metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 (L858R) substitution mutations (first-line, maintenance, or after >=1 prior chemotherapy)
First-line locally advanced, unresectable or metastatic pancreatic cancer, in combination with gemcitabine

dosage.n: Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity
Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity

dosage.d: Withhold during evaluation; discontinue if ILD confirmed
dosage.n: Median ILD onset ~39 days (range 5 days to >9 months)

dosage.d: Withhold; discontinue if not resolved within 3 weeks
dosage.n: Bilirubin >3x ULN or transaminases >5x ULN: withhold and consider discontinuation

admin: Take orally once daily on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after food
Select NSCLC patients based on documented EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 (L858R) mutation
Avoid concomitant proton pump inhibitors; stagger antacids and H2 blockers
Advise patients not to smoke (smoking lowers erlotinib exposure)
Continue treatment until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
moa: Reversibly inhibits the kinase activity of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), preventing autophosphorylation of tyrosine residues and blocking downstream signaling that drives tumor cell survival and proliferation. Binding affinity is higher for EGFR exon 19 deletion and exon 21 (L858R) mutant receptors than for wild-type EGFR.

relative: Pregnancy / females of reproductive potential not using contraception
Pre-existing hepatic impairment or biliary obstruction

preg: Based on animal data and mechanism of action, erlotinib can cause fetal harm; animal studies showed embryo-fetal lethality and abortion. Advise pregnant women of risk and females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during and after treatment.
lact: There are no data on erlotinib in human milk; because of potential for serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment.
renal: Pharmacokinetics in patients with compromised renal function is unknown. Monitor renal function and electrolytes, particularly in patients at risk of dehydration; withhold for severe (grade 3-4) renal toxicity.
hepatic: Hepatotoxicity, including hepatic failure and hepatorenal syndrome, can occur with or without pre-existing impairment. Erlotinib is cleared primarily by the liver; exposure was similar in moderate impairment (Child-Pugh B). Monitor LFTs periodically; withhold or discontinue for severe or worsening liver tests.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, voriconazole, grapefruit) - increase erlotinib exposure/toxicity; avoid or reduce dose
Combined CYP3A4/CYP1A2 inhibitor ciprofloxacin - increased exposure
Proton pump inhibitors (omeprazole) - decrease erlotinib exposure; avoid
Warfarin / coumarin anticoagulants - increased INR and bleeding; monitor INR
moderate: CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, St. John's wort) - decrease exposure; increase dose if unavoidable
H2-receptor antagonists / antacids (ranitidine) - decrease exposure; modify dosing schedule
minor: Drugs altering gastric pH generally reduce erlotinib absorption
interactions.food: Food increases bioavailability to ~100% - take on empty stomach. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice (CYP3A4 inhibition).
interactions.alcohol: No specific systemic interaction documented; use alcohol-free emollient creams for treatment-related skin reactions.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate transaminases and bilirubin; can prolong INR in patients on warfarin.

serious: Interstitial lung disease (ILD), including fatal cases (~1.1%)
rare: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with thrombocytopenia (pancreatic cancer)
emergency: Acute or progressive unexplained dyspnea/cough/fever (possible ILD)

monitoring: Renal function and electrolytes, especially with dehydration risk
Pulmonary symptoms for early ILD detection
INR regularly in patients on warfarin or coumarin anticoagulants
counsel: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after eating
Report immediately any new or worsening shortness of breath, cough or fever
Report severe diarrhea (manage with loperamide), severe abdominal pain, or yellowing of skin/eyes
Use sunscreen and alcohol-free emollients; seek care for severe or blistering skin reactions
Do not smoke; smoking reduces drug effectiveness
Use effective contraception and do not breastfeed
pk: EGFR inhibition rapid; tumor response over weeks
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions 15-30 C
pearls: ILD is a defining serious toxicity: median onset ~39 days; discontinue permanently if confirmed
Hepatotoxicity (including fatal hepatic failure/hepatorenal syndrome) mandates routine LFT monitoring
Rash severity often correlates with response but manage proactively
Smoking and PPIs both lower erlotinib exposure and can reduce efficacy
Reserve for tumors with confirmed sensitizing EGFR mutations in NSCLC
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered on an empty stomach unless it is almost time for the next dose; do not take two doses on the same day. Resume the regular once-daily schedule.
overdose: Withhold erlotinib in patients with overdose or suspected overdose and institute symptomatic and supportive treatment. There is no specific antidote.
